summary: Ran a live Jev (Typesafe) evaluation against five past transcripts (~15.7k input tokens, 7 questions each in parallel), saved full answers to the gitignored .artifacts/jev-eval.json, then deleted the temporary scripts/jev-eval.mjs after capture. Followed up by enumerating global vs project-local skill directories and .env locations to plan making the typesafe-ai skill and TYPESAFE_API_KEY accessible across ncp/cronkis.
decisions: Used a one-off scripts/jev-eval.mjs (raw fetch against Typesafe, no SDK install) to avoid adding dependencies to the gizmo project for a single review run.
Ran Jev in parallel across 5 transcripts (gizmo-0128, gizmo-0131, gizmo-0126, ncp-0115, cronkis-0080) with 7 questions each, 7000-char excerpt cap per transcript.
Removed the temporary scripts/jev-eval.mjs after the run, keeping only .artifacts/jev-eval.json (already covered by .gitignore).

Recorded high-level recommendations: one-intent-per-turn prompting template; log model + reason per task to split strong vs cheap tiers; require verification_done before declaring work done; explicitly invoke unity-docs and writing-for-agents skills; install typesafe-ai globally and propagate .env access to ncp/cronkis.
Chose ~/.agents/skills (already contains a typesafe-ai entry from Sep 16) over ~/.claude/skills or ~/.gizmo/skills as the global skill home for typesafe-ai.
